items.headline: Eight biotechnology companies leading the charge in Poland
items.preview: Poland's biotech industry is rapidly evolving, with eight key companies at the forefront.
items.article:
Over the last decade, Poland has seen the rise of its biotech industry. While the country’s pharmaceutical industry has traditionally focused on developing generics, many of these companies have started moving towards developing biologics. Meanwhile, biotech startups in Poland are working on developing new technologies, with a strong focus on treatments for cancer and autoimmune disease. 
Why this matters: As the country sees success stories in its biotech sector, more and more academics and entrepreneurs have been encouraged to start a business in Poland’s biotech industry. This growth is crucial for enhancing healthcare solutions and fostering innovation in the region.

items.headline: Can Stem Cell Treatment for Diabetes in Japan Improve Insulin Independence?
items.preview: Stem cell treatments in Japan show promise for improving insulin independence in diabetes patients.
items.article:
Stem cell treatment for diabetes in Japan can significantly improve insulin independence by regenerating damaged tissues and reducing inflammation. While it is rarely a total cure, many patients experience a 30% to 50% reduction in insulin needs and better blood sugar control under Japan’s strict safety regulations. 
Why this matters: These innovative treatments aim to address the root causes of pancreatic dysfunction, moving beyond symptom management and offering new hope for diabetes patients.

items.headline: Inside Takeda’s transformation: The pipeline strategy behind its next growth chapter
items.preview: Takeda is restructuring to enhance its pipeline and replace revenue from aging products.
items.article:
With a major restructuring underway, Japanese pharma giant Takeda is entering a defining period for its business. Having completed years of portfolio reshaping following its acquisition of Shire in 2019, the company now faces a new challenge: replacing revenue from ageing products while proving that its next generation of medicines can sustain long-term growth. 
Why this matters: Takeda's ambitious transformation plan aims to sharpen its competitive edge and accelerate growth, focusing on high-value late-stage pipeline assets to ensure sustainable revenue.

items.headline: How Can Stem Cell Injections Help Knee Pain in Japan?
items.preview: Stem cell injections in Japan offer a promising solution for knee pain and osteoarthritis.
items.article:
Stem cell injections for knee pain in Japan are a minimally invasive regenerative treatment leveraging the country’s stringent regulations to repair damaged cartilage and reduce inflammation. Patients often experience significant improvements in mobility and pain reduction, with an approximate 80% success rate for mild to moderate osteoarthritis cases. 
Why this matters: This innovative therapy provides a non-surgical option for patients suffering from chronic joint discomfort, enhancing their quality of life and potentially delaying the need for knee replacement surgery.

items.headline: Realistic monkey body animation reveals an uncanny valley in macaque body perception
items.preview: A new study explores how macaques perceive animated bodies, revealing an uncanny valley effect.
items.article:
Social interactions are essential for survival in primates, relying on both facial expressions and body signals. The accurate characterization of these signals is critical for understanding the neurocomputational mechanisms underlying social communication. A new study developed MacAction, a realistic macaque body avatar animated from multi-camera markerless tracking data. 
Why this matters: The findings support the commonalities of social vision across primate species and provide a foundation for controlled experiments aimed at clarifying the detailed neurocomputational mechanisms of social body perception.
